Spoofing.description: Identity Spoofing - Impersonating legitimate users, services, or system components.

Tampering.description: Data Tampering - Unauthorized modification of data at rest, data in transit, or code integrity.

Repudiation.description: Repudiation - Performing actions without accountability, auditability, or non-repudiation tracing.

Information Disclosure.description: Information Disclosure - Leakage, interception, or unauthorized access to sensitive or confidential data.

Denial of Service.description: Denial of Service - Resource exhaustion, service disruption, or degradation of system availability.

Elevation of Privilege.description: Elevation of Privilege - Gaining capabilities, access, or permissions beyond authorized levels.

dfd_properties.is_encrypted: Encrypted communication channel in transit (e.g., TLS/HTTPS)
dfd_properties.encrypted_at_rest: Data encrypted at rest in persistent storage
dfd_properties.sanitizes_input: Sanitization and validation of untrusted input parameters
dfd_properties.checks_input_bounds: Strict verification of input buffer boundaries and payload sizes
dfd_properties.authenticates_source: Mutual authentication of the data flow origin
dfd_properties.validates_session_tokens: Integrity validation and rotation of session tokens
dfd_properties.enforces_authorization: Role- or attribute-based access control (RBAC / ABAC)
dfd_properties.runs_as_least_privilege: Execution under the principle of least privilege
dfd_properties.generates_audit_logs: Generation of immutable audit trails and security logs
dfd_properties.is_tamper_evident: Tamper-evident protection and verified integrity for logs
dfd_properties.has_rate_limiting: Rate limiting and request throttling mechanisms
dfd_properties.defines_timeout: Explicit connection and read/write timeouts configured
dfd_properties.enforces_quota_limits: Storage volume quotas and automated data retention policies
dfd_properties.masks_sensitive_data: Masking, tokenization, or redaction of sensitive data in logs and outputs
dfd_properties.restricts_command_execution: Restriction of arbitrary operating system command execution
dfd_properties.enforces_access_control: Strict access control lists (ACLs) and write permissions on storage
dfd_properties.crosses_trust_boundary: Data flow crosses an architectural trust boundary (e.g., Internet to internal)
dfd_properties.masks_error_details: Secure exception handling without leaking stack traces or internal runtime details
dfd_properties.validates_resource_ownership: Strict resource ownership validation on data access (BOLA/IDOR prevention)
dfd_properties.validates_outgoing_urls: Validation and restriction of outbound destination URLs (SSRF prevention)
dfd_properties.manages_secrets_securely: Use of dedicated secrets vaults without hardcoded or plaintext credentials
dfd_properties.has_backup_and_replication: Periodic automated backups and active multi-region replication
dfd_properties.is_trusted_party: External entity verified and belonging to a trusted domain
dfd_properties.validates_redirect_targets: Validation of destination URLs in HTTP redirects (Open Redirect prevention)
dfd_properties.enforces_strict_cors: Strict CORS policy enforcing origin whitelisting and credential restrictions
dfd_properties.uses_safe_deserializers: Exclusive use of safe serializers and parsers without arbitrary code execution
dfd_properties.verifies_payload_signature: Cryptographic signature validation on payloads and webhooks (e.g., HMAC)
dfd_properties.filters_assignable_properties: Strict filtering of assignable model attributes (Mass Assignment prevention)
dfd_properties.sanitizes_file_paths: Sanitization and canonical path resolution on filesystem access (Path Traversal prevention)
dfd_properties.validates_file_types: Strict validation of allowed extensions and magic bytes in file uploads

rules.title: Unauthenticated Process or API Endpoint
rules.description: Endpoints or processes without enforced authentication allow untrusted adversaries to forge requests and impersonate legitimate clients.
rules.mitigation: Enforce strong authentication mechanisms (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT or API Keys) before executing business logic.

rules.title: Missing Mutual Authentication on Data Flow
rules.description: The communication channel does not authenticate the origin of the data flow, enabling man-in-the-middle spoofing attacks.
rules.mitigation: Implement mutual TLS (mTLS) or signed request tokens to authenticate the source component.

rules.title: Weak or Unvalidated Session Identifiers
rules.description: The process does not properly validate or rotate session identifiers, leaving it susceptible to session hijacking or fixation.
rules.mitigation: Use cryptographically random session tokens, invalidate them on logout, and bind them securely to client context.

rules.title: Untrusted External Entity Impersonation
rules.description: External interactors operating outside the organization trust zone can forge identity or origin headers unless verified as a trusted party.
rules.mitigation: Authenticate external clients via mutual TLS, signed API keys, or identity provider verification, and establish trust boundaries.

rules.title: Unvalidated Redirection Target (Open Redirect)
rules.description: Process performs HTTP redirects using user-supplied parameters without validation, facilitating phishing and credential theft.
rules.mitigation: Maintain an explicit whitelist of allowed redirect URLs and validate targets strictly before initiating redirection.

rules.title: Overly Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)
rules.description: Process configures wildcard origins or insecure CORS policies alongside credentials, allowing malicious external domains to impersonate authenticated browser clients.
rules.mitigation: Restrict allowed origins to an explicit trusted domain whitelist and disallow wildcard origins when credentials are supported.

rules.title: Unencrypted Dataflow Subject to In-Transit Tampering
rules.description: Data flowing over an unencrypted or unauthenticated transport channel can be altered or injected in transit by an adversary.
rules.mitigation: Ensure data flows enforce TLS 1.3 encryption with cryptographic integrity verification (HMAC / AEAD).

rules.title: Untrusted Input Sanitization and Injection Vulnerability
rules.description: Input from external sources is processed without strict sanitization, allowing SQL, Command, or Template Injection.
rules.mitigation: Implement strict input validation schemas, parameterized SQL queries, and context-aware output encoding.

rules.title: Missing Input Bounds and Memory Safety Checks
rules.description: Memory manipulation or payload processing lacks boundary checking, creating buffer overflow or payload mutation risks.
rules.mitigation: Use memory-safe languages or enforce strict length and boundary checks on all inbound buffers and payloads.

rules.title: Unauthorized Datastore Modification
rules.description: The datastore does not enforce strict access control or integrity verification on write operations, risking record tampering.
rules.mitigation: Configure strict database permissions, access control lists (ACLs), and row-level security.

rules.title: Insecure Trust Boundary Crossing without Transport Encryption
rules.description: Data traverses an architectural trust boundary over an unencrypted channel, exposing in-flight data to active packet manipulation and tampering.
rules.mitigation: Mandate TLS 1.3 encryption and message integrity verification (AEAD/HMAC) for all flows crossing trust boundaries.

rules.title: Insecure Object Deserialization
rules.description: Process deserializes untrusted data using unsafe deserializers (such as pickle or unsafe YAML loaders), allowing adversaries to alter internal execution graphs and execute arbitrary code.
rules.mitigation: Use safe data-only serialization formats (JSON, Protobuf) or strictly enforce safe loaders (e.g. yaml.safe_load) without arbitrary class instantiation.

rules.title: Unverified Inbound Webhook Payload Ingestion
rules.description: Webhook ingestion endpoint processes incoming event notifications without validating cryptographic HMAC payload signatures, allowing payload forgery and tampering.
rules.mitigation: Verify HMAC signatures (e.g., Stripe-Signature, X-Hub-Signature) against shared secrets before processing webhook events.

rules.title: Missing Security Audit Logging
rules.description: Critical business transactions and security state transitions occur without generating audit trails, allowing actors to repudiate actions.
rules.mitigation: Implement non-repudiable audit logging for sensitive operations including identity, timestamp, action, and outcome.

rules.title: Mutable or Tamperable Audit Log Storage
rules.description: Logs or audit stores can be modified or deleted by privileged or compromised processes, undermining accountability.
rules.mitigation: Send logs to write-once-read-many (WORM) storage, centralized append-only log services, or use cryptographic log chaining.

rules.title: Unauthenticated Operations by External Entity
rules.description: External entity executes actions or sends data without mandatory authentication or signature, preventing non-repudiation and forensic tracing.
rules.mitigation: Enforce client identity authentication, cryptographic request signatures, and audit timestamps at entry gateways.

rules.title: Cleartext Sensitive Data in Transit
rules.description: Data transmission lacks transport layer encryption, exposing sensitive payloads and authentication tokens to network eavesdropping.
rules.mitigation: Enforce HTTPS/TLS encryption across all network boundaries and disallow unencrypted legacy protocols.

rules.title: Unencrypted Sensitive Data at Rest
rules.description: The datastore does not enforce encryption at rest, exposing records if storage media, backups, or underlying instances are compromised.
rules.mitigation: Enable storage volume encryption (AES-256) and field-level encryption for high-sensitivity data.

rules.title: Insecure Protocol Usage
rules.description: The data flow uses an inherently unencrypted or obsolete protocol such as HTTP, FTP, Telnet, or unencrypted WebSockets.
rules.mitigation: Upgrade protocol configuration to secure variants (HTTPS, SFTP, SSH, WSS).

rules.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information in Unmasked Storage
rules.description: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or credentials stored without data masking or tokenization risk exposure to unauthorized internal staff.
rules.mitigation: Implement pseudonymization, data masking, and tokenization for sensitive personal attributes.

rules.title: Verbose Error Details and Stack Trace Disclosure
rules.description: Process does not mask internal runtime exceptions, exposing stack traces, framework versions, and database schemas in error responses.
rules.mitigation: Implement centralized error-handling middleware that returns generic error messages to clients while logging stack traces internally.

rules.title: Insecure Secrets Management and Credential Exposure
rules.description: Secrets, database credentials, or private keys are not managed via dedicated secrets vaults, risking exposure via source code, logs, or environment dumping.
rules.mitigation: Use dedicated secrets managers (HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) and avoid storing credentials in plain environment variables.

rules.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability
rules.description: Process fetches remote resources based on user-supplied URLs without restricting target IP addresses, enabling internal cloud metadata probing.
rules.mitigation: Validate and whitelist target URLs, disable HTTP redirects on outbound clients, and block private IP address ranges (RFC 1918, link-local 169.254.169.254).

rules.title: Path Traversal and Arbitrary File Disclosure
rules.description: Process resolves file system paths using untrusted user input without canonicalization, enabling directory traversal to read arbitrary system files or application code.
rules.mitigation: Validate input against an allowlist, use canonical path resolution (e.g., Path.resolve()), and verify paths stay within authorized base directories.

rules.title: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption and Missing Rate Limiting
rules.description: The process handles inbound traffic without rate limiting or request throttling, enabling denial of service via resource exhaustion.
rules.mitigation: Implement rate limiting algorithms (token bucket, leaky bucket) at the API gateway or application layer.

rules.title: Missing Connection Timeout Configuration
rules.description: Data flow does not define explicit connection and read timeouts, enabling slowloris or socket starvation attacks.
rules.mitigation: Configure strict connection, handshake, and read/write timeouts on all networking clients and servers.

rules.title: Datastore Capacity Exhaustion
rules.description: Datastores without data retention limits or volume quotas can be exhausted by continuous writes, crashing dependent applications.
rules.mitigation: Set disk quotas, automated retention policies, and monitoring alerts for storage capacity.

rules.title: Datastore Unavailability and Data Loss from Missing Backups
rules.description: Datastore lacks automated backups and multi-region replication, leading to permanent denial of service and data loss during hardware failure or ransomware.
rules.mitigation: Enable automated daily snapshots, point-in-time recovery (PITR), and cross-region replication for persistent data stores.

rules.title: Missing Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)
rules.description: Process executes with elevated operating system or cluster privileges, allowing an attacker who breaches it to compromise the entire host.
rules.mitigation: Run processes as dedicated unprivileged system users, drop root capabilities, and apply container security profiles.

rules.title: Missing Authorization and Role-Based Access Control
rules.description: Operations and routes lack role-based authorization checks, allowing authenticated low-privilege users to access administrative features.
rules.mitigation: Enforce strict server-side authorization checks on every operation (Broken Object Level Authorization - BOLA prevention).

rules.title: Unrestricted System Command Execution
rules.description: Process retains the ability to spawn subshells or run arbitrary system commands, opening doors to privilege escalation via shell escapes.
rules.mitigation: Avoid invoking shell commands; use native programming libraries and restrict command execution via sandboxing or seccomp.

rules.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA / IDOR)
rules.description: Process does not validate that the authenticated user possesses ownership or access rights over the requested object ID, enabling privilege escalation across tenants.
rules.mitigation: Enforce resource-level authorization checks validating caller ownership before retrieving or mutating records by ID.

rules.title: Mass Assignment via Unfiltered Object Properties
rules.description: Process binds client-supplied parameters directly to internal data models without property filtering, allowing attackers to escalate privileges by injecting unauthorized attributes.
rules.mitigation: Enforce strict Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) or Pydantic schemas that whitelist explicitly assignable fields for mutations.

rules.title: Arbitrary File Upload and Execution Vulnerability
rules.description: Process accepts file uploads without verifying allowed file extensions or MIME magic numbers, enabling upload and execution of malicious server scripts.
rules.mitigation: Validate file extensions and magic bytes against a strict whitelist, store files outside public web roots, and disable execution permissions.
